01.event: Sent by Rav Hisda to ostracize the Elders of Nezonya for skipping his lecture, Rav Hamnuna asked why and they posed a question he could not answer.
01.turn: The Elders mocked him by renaming him Karnuna (a cold fish) after he could not answer their question about a castrated slave.
01.outcome: He returned to Rav Hisda, who told him the question is answered by a baraita he should have known.
01.summary: The Elders of Nezonya stopped attending Rav Hisda's lecture, so he sent Rav Hamnuna to ostracize them. They told Hamnuna they had asked Rav Hisda a question he never resolved, and Hamnuna invited them to ask him instead. When he could not answer their question about a castrated slave, they mocked his name. He went back to Rav Hisda, who pointed out that a baraita answers it.

02.event: On his deathbed Mar Ukva asked for his charity records and found he had given seven thousand dinars.
02.turn: He judged this too little to carry him to the World-to-Come.
02.outcome: He got up and gave away half of his remaining wealth to charity.
02.summary: As Mar Ukva lay dying, he asked for his charity records and saw he had given seven thousand gold dinars. He said his provisions were light and the road long. So he rose and gave half of his remaining money to charity.

03.event: At his son's wedding, Rava served drinks to the guests, and Rav Pappa and Rav Huna stood for him while Rav Mari and Rav Pineḥas did not.
03.turn: Rava grew angry at those who stayed seated.
03.outcome: He rebuked them, asking whether some Sages count as Sages and others do not.
03.summary: Rava served drinks at his son's wedding feast. Two sages, Rav Pappa and Rav Huna, stood up when he poured for them, but Rav Mari and Rav Pineḥas stayed seated. Rava became angry and asked whether those who stood were Sages and those who sat were not.

04.event: The priestly court raised the marriage contract for priests' widows to two hundred because the priests were demeaning them.
04.turn: Men then avoided marrying priestly widows and preferred Israelite virgins at the same price.
04.outcome: The court restored the earlier arrangement.
04.summary: A court of priests first set a virgin's contract at four hundred and a widow's at one hundred. Seeing priests demean widows, it raised the widow's sum to two hundred. When grooms then stayed away and married Israelite virgins instead, the court restored the original arrangement.
04.missing: This is an institutional history used to reconcile two legal sources, with no individual characters or specific scene.

05.event: A man asking for charity told Rabbi Neḥemya he normally dined on fatty meat and aged wine, and Neḥemya invited him to share lentils.
05.turn: The man ate the lentils and, unaccustomed to such food, died.
05.outcome: Neḥemya said woe to the one he had killed, which the Gemara reads as blaming the man for pampering himself.
05.summary: A man came to Rabbi Neḥemya for charity and said he usually ate fatty meat and aged wine. Neḥemya invited him to eat lentils with him. The man ate them and died, being unused to simple food. Neḥemya exclaimed over him, and the Gemara explains the man should not have pampered himself so much.

06.event: Ameimar permitted Rav Huna bar Natan to marry a woman from Meḥoza, and Rav Ashi challenged his reasoning.
06.turn: Rav Ashi pointed out that several academies did not teach the ruling Ameimar relied on.
06.outcome: Ameimar did not accept the challenge because he had the ruling directly from Rav Zevid of Neharde'a.
06.summary: Ameimar allowed Rav Huna bar Natan to marry a woman from Meḥoza. Rav Ashi asked what his reasoning was and noted that the schools of Rav Kahana, Rav Pappa and Rav Zevid did not teach that ruling. Ameimar did not accept the objection, since he had heard the ruling from Rav Zevid himself.
06.missing: This is mostly a legal exchange about a ruling; the human event is only gestured at.

07.missing: The passage is a question Rabbi Elazar poses to an elder about the timing of a ruling, with no event or outcome.

08.actor: A man testifying before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
08.event: A man came to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi claiming another man was a Levite because he had been called second to read the Torah.
08.turn: The rabbi asked whether that order reflected Levite status or simply prominence, and the man answered that a priest had read before him.
08.outcome: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi accepted the testimony and elevated the man to Levite status.
08.summary: A man told Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi that another man was a Levite, because he read second at the synagogue. The rabbi asked if that was due to Levite status or to being a great man. The man replied that a priest had read before him. The rabbi then accepted the claim and recognized the man as a Levite.

09.event: When the exiles returned from Babylonia they encamped by the Heker well, and the prophets among them permitted drawing from it on a Festival.
09.turn: The text then corrects itself: it was really an inherited custom from their forefathers.
09.outcome: The permission stood as an ancestral practice.
09.summary: The returning exiles camped by this well, and their prophets permitted them to use it on a Festival. The text says this was really an inherited custom that the prophets allowed them to continue.
09.missing: It is a brief historical note supporting a legal point, not a developed episode.

10.event: While Rabbi Elazar and Reish Lakish sat before Rabbi Yoḥanan, a case like the earlier one arose, and Reish Lakish again asked whether the man had received a share at the threshing floor.
10.turn: Rabbi Yoḥanan gave the answer Rabbi Elazar had earlier voiced, showing it was Yoḥanan's own teaching.
10.outcome: Reish Lakish glared at Rabbi Elazar and reproached him for not saying it in his teacher's name.
10.summary: Earlier, Reish Lakish had challenged a priesthood claim and Rabbi Elazar replied that the priesthood does not lapse without a threshing floor. Later, before Rabbi Yoḥanan, a similar case arose, and Reish Lakish raised the same challenge. Yoḥanan gave that very reply, and Reish Lakish realized Elazar had been quoting him. He looked at Elazar harshly and scolded him for not naming his source.

11.event: A man helped Shmuel off a ferry, then said he had a case to bring before him.
11.turn: Shmuel realized the favor created a bond that compromised his impartiality.
11.outcome: Shmuel disqualified himself from judging the man's case.
11.summary: Shmuel was crossing a river by ferry when a man reached out a hand to help him. Shmuel asked what the man was doing there, and the man said he had a case to bring. Shmuel declared himself disqualified from judging it, because the man had done him a favor.

12.actor: A man who sold land to Rav Pappa
12.event: The man sold land to Rav Pappa to raise money for oxen.
12.turn: He ended up not needing the money.
12.outcome: Rav Pappa returned the land to him, which the Gemara says was beyond the letter of the law.
12.summary: A man sold his land to Rav Pappa because he needed money to buy oxen. In the end he did not need the money, and Rav Pappa gave the land back to him. The Gemara says Rav Pappa acted beyond what the law required.

13.actor: The sister of Rami bar Ḥama and Rav Avya
13.event: The sister of Rami bar Ḥama was married to Rav Avya; her marriage contract was lost, and they came before Rav Yosef.
13.turn: Rav Yosef cited a ruling that a man may keep his wife for years without a contract, and Abaye countered with Rav Naḥman's ruling following Rabbi Meir.
13.outcome: Rav Yosef told them to go and write her a new contract.
13.summary: Rami bar Ḥama's sister was married to Rav Avya, and her marriage contract was lost. They came before Rav Yosef, who cited a view that a husband may keep his wife without a contract for years. Abaye objected that the law follows Rabbi Meir's stricter view, and Rav Yosef said that if so, he should go and write her a new contract.
13.missing: The shown passage [4] alone is only the introduction; the incident continues in the following segments, and much of it is legal argument.

14.event: Rav and Rav Yehuda were walking on the road with a woman ahead of them, and Rav told Rav Yehuda to lift his feet away from Gehenna.
14.turn: Rav Yehuda objected that Rav himself permits this for men of fit morals, but Rav said he did not mean men like them.
14.outcome: Rav explained that only men like Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappi and his colleagues qualify.
14.summary: Rav and Rav Yehuda were walking along a road with a woman walking ahead of them. Rav urged Rav Yehuda to hurry away from Gehenna. Rav Yehuda reminded him that Rav allows this for men of fit morals. Rav replied that he did not mean men like the two of them, but people like Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappi and his companions.

15.event: Rabba bar Ḥiyya conducted a ḥalitza using a slipper, alone, and at night.
15.outcome: Shmuel remarked how great is the man who follows an individual opinion.
15.summary: Rabba bar Ḥiyya of Ctesiphon performed a ḥalitza ceremony using a slipper, by himself as the only judge, and at night. Shmuel commented sarcastically on how great this master was, relying on an individual opinion.

16.event: Ulla, who used to travel to Eretz Yisrael, died outside the Land.
16.turn: Rabbi Elazar lamented that Ulla fulfilled the verse about dying in an unclean land, even after being told the coffin was coming.
16.outcome: Rabbi Elazar held that being absorbed by the Land's soil after death is not the same as in life.
16.summary: Ulla often went up to Eretz Yisrael but died abroad. When told, Rabbi Elazar said Ulla had fulfilled the verse that he would die in an unclean land. They answered that his coffin was being brought to the Land, but Rabbi Elazar said being received by its soil after death is not like being received while alive.

17.event: A widow's son asked Rabbi Eliezer whose request to honor first if both parents ask for water, and Rabbi Eliezer said to honor the father.
17.turn: The son went to Rabbi Yehoshua and received the same answer, then asked what if his mother were divorced.
17.outcome: Rabbi Yehoshua sarcastically told him to pour water for both and squawk at them like chickens, noting from his tear-filled eyelashes that he was a widow's son.
17.summary: A widow's son asked Rabbi Eliezer which parent to serve first if both ask for water; the rabbi said to put the mother aside and honor the father, since both are obligated to honor him. The son asked Rabbi Yehoshua, who answered the same. When he asked what if his mother were divorced, Rabbi Yehoshua said it was clear from his eyelashes he was a widow's son and sarcastically told him to pour water for both and squawk at them like chickens.

18.event: A heretic cited a verse to claim God had abandoned Israel the way a yavam performs ḥalitza on a yevama.
18.turn: Rabban Gamliel retorted that the verse says Israel removed itself from God, and that ḥalitza has no significance anyway.
18.summary: A heretic told Rabban Gamliel that God had performed ḥalitza on Israel, citing a verse that says God removed Himself from them. Rabban Gamliel called him a fool and pointed out the verse says 'from them,' meaning Israel removed itself from God, and a ḥalitza carries no significance anyway.
18.missing: It is a short polemical exchange of arguments rather than an event with setting or consequence.

19.event: Rav Ḥisda praised Rav Hamnuna to Rav Huna, who asked to see him, and noticed Hamnuna did not cover his head.
19.turn: Hamnuna explained he was unmarried, and Rav Huna was displeased.
19.outcome: Rav Huna turned his face away and told him not to see his face until he married.
19.summary: Rav Ḥisda praised Rav Hamnuna to Rav Huna as a great man, and Rav Huna asked to meet him. When Hamnuna arrived without a head covering, he explained that he was not married. Rav Huna turned away from him and said not to appear before him again until he had married.

20.missing: The passage only comments on the preceding story with Rabbi Abba's and Rabbi Ḥanina's theological statements and verse proofs; no event happens in it.
